title: Ensure 'Enable computer and user accounts to be trusted for delegation' is set to 'No One'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment\Enable computer and user accounts to be trusted for delegation to 'No One'
reason: Misuse of this user right could allow unauthorized users to impersonate other users on the network.

title: Ensure 'Force shutdown from a remote system' is set to 'Administrators'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment\Force shutdown from a remote system to 'Administrators'
reason: Any user who can shut down a computer could cause a DoS condition to occur.

title: Ensure 'Generate security audits' is set to 'LOCAL SERVICE, NETWORK SERVICE, RESTRICTED SERVICES\PrintSpoolerService'
expected: LOCAL SERVICE, NETWORK SERVICE, RESTRICTED SERVICES\PrintSpoolerService
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment\Generate security audits to 'LOCAL SERVICE, NETWORK SERVICE, RESTRICTED SERVICES\PrintSpoolerService'
reason: A threat actor could use this capability to create a large number of audited events, which would make it more difficult for a system administrator to locate any illicit activity.

title: Ensure 'Impersonate a client after authentication' is set to 'Administrators, LOCAL SERVICE, NETWORK SERVICE, SERVICE, RESTRICTED SERVICES\PrintSpoolerService'
expected: Administrators, LOCAL SERVICE, NETWORK SERVICE, SERVICE, RESTRICTED SERVICES\PrintSpoolerService
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment\Impersonate a client after authentication to 'Administrators, LOCAL SERVICE, NETWORK SERVICE, SERVICE, RESTRICTED SERVICES\PrintSpoolerService'
reason: A threat actor with the Impersonate a client after authentication user right could create a service, trick a client to make them connect to the service, and then impersonate that client to elevate the threat actor's level of access.

title: Ensure 'Impersonate a client after authentication' is set to 'Administrators, LOCAL SERVICE, NETWORK SERVICE, SERVICE, RESTRICTED SERVICES\PrintSpoolerService'
expected: Administrators, LOCAL SERVICE, NETWORK SERVICE, SERVICE, RESTRICTED SERVICES\PrintSpoolerService
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment\Impersonate a client after authentication to 'Administrators, LOCAL SERVICE, NETWORK SERVICE, SERVICE, RESTRICTED SERVICES\PrintSpoolerService'
reason: A threat actor with the Impersonate a client after authentication user right could create a service, trick a client to make them connect to the service, and then impersonate that client to elevate the threat actor's level of access.

title: Ensure 'Increase scheduling priority' is set to 'Administrators, Window Manager\Window Manager Group'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment\Increase scheduling priority to 'Administrators, Window Manager\Window Manager Group'
reason: A user who is assigned this user right could increase the scheduling priority of a process to Real-Time, which would leave little processing time for all other processes and could lead to a DoS condition.

title: Ensure 'Load and unload device drivers' is set to 'Administrators'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment\Load and unload device drivers to 'Administrators'
reason: A user or threat actor who has the Load and unload device drivers user right could unintentionally install malicious code that masquerades as a device driver.

title: Ensure 'Lock pages in memory' is set to 'No One'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment\Lock pages in memory to 'No One'
reason: Users with the Lock pages in memory user right could assign physical memory to several processes, which could leave little or no RAM for other processes and result in a DoS condition.

title: Ensure 'Log on as a batch job' is set to 'Administrators'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment\Log on as a batch job to 'Administrators'
reason: Its use should be restricted in high security environments to prevent misuse of system resources or to prevent threat actors from using the right to launch malicious code.

title: Ensure 'Manage auditing and security log' is set to 'Administrators'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment\Manage auditing and security log to 'Administrators'
reason: Anyone with this user right can clear the Security log to erase important evidence of unauthorized activity.

title: Ensure 'Manage auditing and security log' is set to 'Administrators'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment\Manage auditing and security log to 'Administrators'
reason: Anyone with this user right can clear the Security log to erase important evidence of unauthorized activity.

title: Ensure 'Modify an object label' is set to 'No One'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment\Modify an object label to 'No One'
reason: By modifying the integrity label of an object owned by another user a threat actor may cause them to execute code at a higher level of privilege than intended.

title: Ensure 'Modify firmware environment values' is set to 'Administrators'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment\Modify firmware environment values to 'Administrators'
reason: Anyone who is assigned the Modify firmware environment values user right could configure the settings of a hardware component to cause it to fail, which could lead to data corruption or a DoS condition.

title: Ensure 'Perform volume maintenance tasks' is set to 'Administrators'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment\Perform volume maintenance tasks to 'Administrators'
reason: A user who is assigned the Perform volume maintenance tasks user right could delete a volume, which could result in the loss of data or a DoS condition.

title: Ensure 'Profile single process' is set to 'Administrators'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment\Profile single process to 'Administrators'
reason: A threat actor with this user right could monitor a computer's performance to help identify critical processes that they might wish to attack directly.

title: Ensure 'Profile system performance' is set to 'Administrators, NT SERVICE\WdiServiceHost'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment\Profile system performance to 'Administrators, NT SERVICE\WdiServiceHost'
reason: Threat actors with this user right could monitor a computer's performance to help identify critical processes that they might wish to attack directly.

title: Ensure 'Replace a process level token' is set to 'LOCAL SERVICE, NETWORK SERVICE'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment\Replace a process level token to 'LOCAL SERVICE, NETWORK SERVICE'
reason: Users with the Replace a process level token privilege are able to start processes as other users whose credentials they know.

title: Ensure 'Restore files and directories' is set to 'Administrators'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment\Restore files and directories to 'Administrators'
reason: A threat actor with the Restore files and directories user right could restore sensitive data to a computer and overwrite data that is more recent, which could lead to loss of important data.

title: Ensure 'Shut down the system' is set to 'Administrators'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment\Shut down the system to 'Administrators'
reason: Misuse of this user right can result in a denial-of-service condition.

title: Ensure 'Synchronize directory service data' is set to 'No One'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment\Synchronize directory service data to 'No One'
reason: Threat actors who have this user right can view all information stored within the directory.

title: Ensure 'Take ownership of files or other objects' is set to 'Administrators'
remediation: Set GP: Computer Configuration\Policies\Windows Settings\Security Settings\Local Policies\User Rights Assignment\Take ownership of files or other objects to 'Administrators'
reason: Any users with the Take ownership of files or other objects user right can take control of any object, regardless of the permissions on that object, and then make any changes they wish to that object.
